passage:
"Vaibhav, time to go home now."
"No! Swing!"
"One more push, then home."
Yamini gave one push. "Okay, all done."
"No! No! Swing!"
Vaibhav's face crumpled. His hands gripped the chains. His legs went stiff.
"Come, baby. Mumma's here."
"Nooo!"
He started to cry, big tears rolling down.

qa.q: What did Vaibhav say when told it was time to go home?
What was Vaibhav feeling when his face crumpled?
qa.a: He felt sad and angry about leaving, and he could not handle the wish to stay.

qa.q: What could Yamini do at this first moment?
qa.a: She could name his feeling, like "You love the swing," and give a simple warning before leaving, staying calm as he cries.

qa.q: How might Yamini be feeling as Vaibhav starts crying?
qa.a: She may feel tired or worried about the scene, but she can see he is only little and upset.

grounding: It shows a toddler told it is time to leave the park who cannot manage the wish to stay, so his face crumples, his body stiffens and he cries.

passage:
Babysitter's note, Thursday.
At the park at five, I told Uday it was time to go. He was in the sandpit. He looked up, and his lip started to shake. He held his spade tight. When I held out my hand, he went stiff all over and threw his head back. Then he cried loudly. I knelt and said, "You wanted to stay. It's hard to go."
— Harsha

qa.q: Where was Uday when it was time to go?
What did Uday's shaking lip show?
qa.a: It showed he was getting upset and frustrated at having to leave.

qa.q: What did Harsha do that helped?
qa.a: Harsha knelt and named Uday's feeling, which helps a toddler feel understood.

qa.q: How might Uday's parents feel reading the note?
qa.a: They may feel reassured that Harsha stayed kind and calm when Uday got upset.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler told to leave the park who cannot manage wanting to stay, so his lip shakes, his body stiffens and he cries.
